item.title: Nigeria 2027 Election Watch: The Ballot Is Taking Shape, But The Political Ground Is Still Moving
item.description: Nigeria’s 2027 elections are approaching a particularly interesting stage. For months, the political conversation has been dominated by defections, coalition-building, candidate selection and arguments about which party controls which state. Now, another picture is emerging. The Independent National Electoral Commission is beginning to settle disputes over who can appear on the ballot. Political parties are still exchanging members and campaign organisers. And INEC is preparing to test the technology that will determine how millions of Nigerians are accredited and how election results are transmitted. Three developments over the weekend illustrate these different dimensions of the approaching elections. In Adamawa, the movement of politicians between parties has continued, this time with a group of APC members joining the Allied Peoples Movement. In Imo, the state electoral commission has postponed its local-government elections indefinitely. And nationally, INEC has published revised candidate lists, clarifying some disputed nominations while leaving others unresolved. These developments tell us something important. Nigeria’s electoral machinery is taking shape. But the political structures seeking to use that machinery are still changing. That is this weekend’s Political Signal. ADAMAWA: THE DEFECTIONS ARE NO LONGER ONE-WAY TRAFFIC Only recently, Adamawa appeared to be experiencing a major consolidation of political officeholders around the APC. Governor Ahmadu Fintiri had moved from the PDP to the ruling party. All 21 local-government chairmen and 226 councillors elected on the PDP platform subsequently followed him. For the APC, that represented an expansion of its network of elected local officials. Adamawa Governor Umaru Fintiri For the PDP, it meant losing the party affiliation of officials who had won office under its banner. But politics rarely moves in only one direction. On Friday, October 30, former Yola South Local Government Chairman Umar Barkindo announced that he had left the APC for the Allied Peoples Movement. He was accompanied by a group of politicians and supporters reportedly numbering more than 5,000. Barkindo attributed his departure to unresolved disagreements within the APC. The APM governorship candidate, Abduralman Haske, is also a former APC politician. The reported membership figure has not been independently verified. But the involvement of an identifiable former local-government chairman establishes that this is more than an anonymous claim of mass defection. The development complicates Adamawa’s political picture. The APC has gained elected local-government officials who previously belonged to the PDP. The APM is now attracting some politicians from the APC. And the PDP must continue organising after losing a substantial number of its elected council officials. item.title: Nigerians, other foreign graduates to get shorter UK work visa from 2027
item.description: The United Kingdom, UK has announced plans to retain its two-year post-study work visa for international students graduating from selected universities, partially reversing an earlier decision to reduce the duration of the scheme. Under the revised policy, graduates of universities with strong immigration compliance records and employment outcomes will continue to qualify for the two-year Graduate visa, while other international graduates will receive 18 months from January 2027. The UK government disclosed the change in its 2026 Budget, although it has yet to publish the list of qualifying universities or explain how institutions will be assessed. The policy introduces a two-tier system in which the university attended by an international student could determine how long they can remain in Britain after completing their studies. “The government will also increase the duration of the Graduate visa to two years for graduates from high compliance universities where there are strong labour market outcomes,” the Budget document said. The change comes after the government announced plans to reduce the standard Graduate visa from two years to 18 months for bachelor’s and master’s degree holders, effective January 1, 2027. Doctoral graduates will continue to qualify for three years. The development could affect thousands of African students, particularly Nigerians, who constitute a significant proportion of Britain’s international student population and rely on post-study employment opportunities to gain work experience and recover the cost of their education. Nigeria was the UK’s third-largest source of sponsored international students in the year ending June 2026, with 26,060 sponsored study visas issued to Nigerian main applicants, behind China and India. Nigerian nationals also recorded 20,604 approvals under the Graduate route during the period, making them the third-largest nationality group to benefit from the scheme. The Graduate visa allows eligible international students to work or search for employment in Britain without requiring immediate employer sponsorship. However, the visa cannot be extended, and graduates seeking to remain longer must switch to another eligible immigration route, such as the Skilled Worker visa. Students graduating before the end of 2026 can still apply for the existing two-year Graduate visa, while the reduced 18-month duration will apply to applications submitted from January 1, 2027. hile maintaining opportunities for international graduates and professionals considered valuable to the country’s labour market. item.title: Delta reduces inherited debt by N400bn, targets 2027 clearance
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi ASABA — The Delta State Government says it has reduced the state’s inherited debt from N463 billion to N63 billion and is targeting full repayment of the outstanding balance by the first quarter of 2027. The Commissioner for Economic Planning, Mr Sonny Ekedayen, disclosed this at the 2026 budget stakeholders’ engagement held in Asaba on Friday. Ekedayen attributed the reported N400 billion reduction to what he described as the Oborevwori administration’s prudent financial management and responsible use of public resources. He said: “We have been able to reduce our legacy debt from N463 billion to N63 billion. We are also working towards clearing the outstanding balance by the first quarter of 2027. “This achievement reflects the commitment of this administration to prudent financial management and responsible utilisation of public resources.” The commissioner said the state government would prioritise roads and other critical infrastructure in the proposed 2027 budget, citing their importance to economic growth and improved access to communities. He said the state’s expenditure structure currently allocated about 70 per cent to capital projects and 30 per cent to recurrent expenditure, adding that the government intended to sustain the emphasis on capital development in the next budget. The Asagba of Asaba, Prof. Epiphany Azinge, called for greater citizens’ participation in the budget preparation process, while commending the state government for its reported budget performance. Azinge said residents and other stakeholders should be given opportunities to contribute to decisions on projects and programmes that directly affect their communities. Meanwhile, civil society organisations at the engagement welcomed plans by the Delta State House of Assembly to introduce legislation regulating housing issues. They said appropriate legislation would help address challenges in the housing sector and provide a framework for improved regulation. item.title: Customs deploys AI tools to tackle fake news, online scams
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has begun deploying artificial intelligence and digital data-tracking tools to combat fake news and online scams capable of damaging its public image. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, disclosed this at the recently concluded NECCIPR Roundtable 2026 in Lagos. He was represented by the Service’s National Public Relations Officer, Deputy Comptroller Abdullahi Maiwada. Adeniyi said it was important for the Service to ensure that members of the public understood the reasons behind its policies, operations and enforcement activities. Speaking on the theme, “Algorithm Influence and Public Relations,” Maiwada said artificial intelligence had become increasingly important to Customs operations, including risk management and strategic communication. He explained that the technology was being used to assess risks associated with imported goods, classify consignments according to their risk levels and guide appropriate Customs interventions. According to him, AI can also analyse public sentiment and provide insights into how people perceive the activities of the Service. Maiwada said Customs was using available digital platforms to establish facts and working with other relevant agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for spreading misleading information. He said: “The role of AI cannot be overemphasised, especially within our operations. Over the years, AI has been deployed in our core operational duties as well as strategic communication. “AI has also been deployed to aid risk management, which involves assessment of the risks in imported items so that they can be categorised according to their different levels of risk to enable appropriate Customs interventions.” Earlier, the convener of the NECCIPR Roundtable 2026, Nkechi Ali-Balogun, said the event was founded on the belief that public relations professionals should not only manage messages but also play a leading role in shaping national discourse. She said this year’s theme examined the growing influence of algorithms and artificial intelligence on public opinion and the flow of information. “When machines decide what we see, who is really shaping the Nigerian mind? Who now controls the flow of information that shapes what Nigerians believe? We live in a rapidly changing world, powered by AI, where a single algorithm can shape political narratives, throw out conspiracy theories, and dictate what millions read, believe, and share,” Ali-Balogun said. item.title: Adeboye urges journalists to verify stories before publication
item.description: Says misinformation threatens public trust, clarifies prayer-walk photo, Tinubu comment By OLAYINKA LATONA The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, RCCG, Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, has urged journalists and social media influencers to verify information thoroughly before publishing, warning that misinformation could damage reputations and erode public trust. Adeboye spoke at a monthly special thanksgiving service and prayer session organised for social media influencers, creative industry practitioners, content creators and drama ministers at the church’s national headquarters, Throne of Grace Parish, Ebute-Metta, Lagos. He said media practitioners and content creators had a responsibility to investigate claims before disseminating them, noting that unverified reports could mislead the public. The cleric used the occasion to address two claims about him that had circulated in the media. He denied protesting against former President Goodluck Jonathan, explaining that a widely circulated photograph of him in white and green attire carrying a placard was taken during a prayer walk in 2020. According to him, the walk was organised in compliance with an instruction from the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, for churches to hold prayer walks in their neighbourhoods. “It is true I carried a placard. It was a prayer walk. CAN said we should do a prayer walk near our churches. That is what I did in Ebute Meta. A walk is a walk,” he said. Adeboye pointed out that Jonathan left office in 2015, five years before the prayer walk took place during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari. “And everybody swallowed it and believed I protested against Jonathan. Nobody checked,” he said. He also faulted reports that, in his comments on President Bola Tinubu, he had said the President had “done his best”. Adeboye recalled speaking in the United States about the abduction of children in Oriire community, Oyo State, and stating that Tinubu, as Commander-in-Chief, had issued the necessary orders for their rescue. He said his remarks were subsequently presented as an endorsement of the President’s handling of the security situation. “Somebody then reported, ‘Pastor Adeboye said the president has done his best,’ and we all swallowed it. When I said the US should not bomb us anymore, that was not news. When I said the US should help us deal with the terrorists, that was not news. God have mercy on journalists,” he said. Recalling his undergraduate days, Adeboye said he took an elective course in the Mass Communication Department, where he was taught the principles of investigative journalism and the need to establish facts before publishing a report. He urged social media influencers to use their platforms responsibly and avoid circulating information that had not been properly verified. item.title: 325 People Arrested At Palestine Action Protest — UK Police
item.description: British police on Sunday said they had arrested 325 people at a London protest in support of Palestine Action the previous day, ahead of a court appeal over the government’s contentious ban of the group. Demonstrators staged a “mass action” outside the US embassy ahead of the Supreme Court holding a two-day hearing from Wednesday on the UK government’s July 2025 decision to outlaw Palestine Action under anti-terror legislation. The United States also designated Palestine Action as “terrorist” in August, as the administration of President Donald Trump intensifies its campaign against left-wing movements. The British designation puts the group on a blacklist that also includes entities like Palestinian militants Hamas, and made membership of, or support for, Palestine Action a crime punishable by up to 14 years in prison. Pro-Palestinian activists and supporters stage a protest in support of the proscribed group Palestine Action outside the US Embassy in London, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP) It has resulted in more than 4,000 people, including many senior citizens and Holocaust survivors, being arrested for showing their support for the group, according to campaigners and police tallies. “In total, 325 people were arrested yesterday,” London’s Metropolitan Police said in an update Sunday. “The vast majority of arrests — 320 — were for expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act.” A smaller number of protesters also rallied outside the US consulate in the Scottish capital Edinburgh on Saturday, but no arrests were made there at the time. A pro-Palestinian activist holds a placard during a protest in support of the proscribed group Palestine Action outside the US Embassy in London, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP) “Enquiries are ongoing to identify people seen wearing t-shirts and holding banners showing support for a proscribed organisation,” Police Scotland said in a statement shared with AFP on Sunday. “Evidence is being reviewed and further action will be taken as appropriate.” The post 325 People Arrested At Palestine Action Protest — UK Police appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Enugu APC urges residents to verify political claims
item.description: By Dennis Agbo The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Enugu State has urged residents to exercise caution when receiving and sharing political information ahead of the 2027 general elections. The APC Campaign Council’s Spokesperson and Director of Public Communications, Steve Oruruo, made the appeal in a statement titled, “Unmasking the Alarmism of NDC: A Clarion Call for Enugu’s Extra Vigilance.” Oruruo referred to public discussions surrounding the management of Amadeo Event Centre and a proposed town hall meeting involving the New Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi. He said the disagreement over the use of the facility was a matter involving the parties to a private agreement and urged political stakeholders to avoid drawing conclusions about the involvement of the state government without verified information. The APC spokesperson also called on residents to verify reports, particularly those circulating on social media, before accepting or sharing them. He said political discussions ahead of the 2027 elections should focus on candidates’ ideas, policies and capacity to deliver good governance. Oruruo further highlighted the development programmes of Governor Peter Mbah’s administration, expressing confidence that the government’s record would feature prominently in the electoral contest. He urged Ndi Enugu to remain vigilant, promote issue-based political engagement and assess the proposals and records of political parties as the state approaches the 2027 general elections. item.title: ‘I searched and found’ – Pastor Jimmy Odukoya confirms marriage to Pastor Mo Jasmine
item.description: Former Nollywood actor turned cleric, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has confirmed his marriage to his fiancée, Pastor Mo Jasmine. Odukoya made the announcement during a church service, where he invited his new wife onto the altar and introduced her to the congregation. The confirmation comes a day after the cleric hinted that he had found love again, sharing a photograph of his and his fiancée’s hands, both wearing rings. Sharing their love story with the congregation, Odukoya said he had been searching for a suitable partner before finding his wife. “You know, the Bible said it is not good, it said I will find someone suitable. When Adam saw, he said this is the flesh of my flesh, bone of my bone, I was looking and searching, and I found. Some of you saw the post, some people said is it artwork, no it’s my wife; allow me to introduce to you for the first time, Pastor Mrs. Odukoya, a new first lady, my wife. Pastor Mo Odukoya,” he said. The marriage marks a new chapter in Odukoya’s personal life following the end of his previous marriage to Oluwakemi Sade Banjoko. The former couple got married in London in March 2013 and had two children together before their separation. item.title: Adeleke, Oyetola unite to deliver 1.5m votes for Tinubu
item.description: Tompolo donates 30 campaign vehicles, launches 10,000 canvassers By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The re-election campaign of President Bola Tinubu in Osun State received a boost at the weekend as Governor Ademola Adeleke and his predecessor, Adegboyega Oyetola, pledged to work together to secure victory for the President in the 2027 election. The commitment came as the Grand Patron of the President Bola Tinubu Door-to-Door Movement, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, launched 10,000 canvassers and donated 30 campaign vehicles and public address systems to support the mobilisation drive. Speaking at the launch held at Freedom Park, Osogbo, representatives of Adeleke and Oyetola called on political leaders and stakeholders to set aside their differences and work towards delivering the targeted 1.5 million votes for Tinubu in the state. Oyetola, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, who was represented by Bola Oyebamiji, urged the canvassers to approach the assignment with sincerity, discipline and commitment. He cautioned them against hypocrisy, political pretence and complacency, while appealing to political leaders, interest groups and other stakeholders to put aside personal interests and differences. “I appeal to all political leaders, interest groups, individuals and stakeholders to rise above selfish interests, personal ego and political differences. Let us demonstrate that political differences need not prevent us from pursuing a shared national objective. “With unity of purpose, effective grassroots mobilisation and unwavering commitment, we can deliver the 1.5 million votes targeted for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Osun State and secure victory for our party’s candidates at all levels,” he said. In his remarks, Adeleke, who is the state coordinator of the Presidential Campaign Council and was represented by his deputy, Kola Adewusi, described the launch of the canvassers and donation of vehicles as timely for the commencement of the President’s campaign in the state. He urged coalition partners to put aside past disagreements and work together, saying the partnership was focused primarily on the presidential election. “Our gathering is therefore a timely push to gain further momentum in the campaign process. We must therefore forget past disagreements and unite to deliver for the President. “All coalition partners have a duty to overlook all previous relationship antagonism and join hands to deliver between 1.5 to 2 million votes for Mr President,” he said. Earlier, Tompolo, who was represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, Dr Kestin Pondi, said the movement was targeting at least 90 per cent of the votes in Osun for Tinubu. “We know that you are already going to vote for your brother. item.title: Osun group demands arrest of Sowore’s attackers
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo A coalition of civil society organisations in Osun State, The Osun Masterminds (TOM), has condemned the reported attack on the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Mr Omoyele Sowore, in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, and called on security agencies to identify and prosecute those responsible. The group described the incident as a national disgrace and an assault on Nigerians’ rights to participate in politics, express their views and support candidates of their choice. TOM’s Executive Director, Professor Wasiu Oyedokun-Alli, made the position known during the group’s monthly briefing on the state of the nation. He said elections should provide an opportunity for candidates and political parties to present their policies and development plans to the electorate, rather than become occasions for violence and intimidation. “Elections should be a festival of ideas, a peaceful contest of developmental blueprints, and a developmental milestone where the sovereign will of the people is freely expressed,” he said. Oyedokun-Alli called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant agencies to investigate the reported attack and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. “We call on the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services (DSS), and all relevant statutory agencies to rise above partisan politics and uphold the rule of law,” he said. The group expressed concern that the political environment was becoming increasingly hostile to opposition figures and Nigerians expressing dissenting views. It alleged that the electoral space was being turned into a combat zone where opposition figures and dissenting voices were targeted, silenced and physically assaulted. Describing the reported attack as a national disgrace, particularly because it allegedly occurred in a public space, TOM also criticised what it said were attempts by security agencies and law enforcement authorities to downplay attacks on political figures. “When security apparatuses and law enforcement agencies trivialize such high-profile acts of violence—dismissing life-threatening injuries as ‘minor’ or engaging in administrative denials—they surrender their neutrality and embolden the forces of tyranny,” the group stated. Oyedokun-Alli warned that Nigeria could not guarantee credible, free and fair elections in 2027 if political violence was allowed to prevent candidates from campaigning and engaging with voters. item.title: Lagos begins joint enforcement of badges for Danfo operators
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Lagos State Government has announced plans to commence joint enforcement of compulsory identification badges and other regulatory requirements for commercial bus operators, popularly known as Danfo drivers and conductors, to strengthen commuter safety and accountability. The enforcement drive, being coordinated by the State Ministry of Transportation through its Directorate of Public Transport and Commuter Services (PTCS), will involve the Vehicle Inspection Service (VIS) and the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA). The Director of Public Transport and Commuter Services, Mr Nuhman Edu, said the initiative was designed to improve commuter security, ensure accountability among transport operators and strengthen compliance with established transport regulations. He identified some of the major compliance gaps the exercise would address to include improper commuter vehicle registration, absence of vehicle body tags, stage carriage permits, drivers’ badges and conductors’ badges. Edu explained that the collaboration with VIS and LASTMA would strengthen the verification of relevant safety documents during routine enforcement operations. “Where a vehicle is found to be non-compliant, enforcement or compliance procedures will be initiated strictly in accordance with extant laws, regulations, approved guidelines and established operational procedures,” he said. He said proper identification of commercial vehicles, drivers and conductors would make operators traceable, improve accountability, assist investigations involving vehicles allegedly used in criminal activities and facilitate the prompt resolution of commuter complaints. According to him, the framework will clearly define the responsibilities of the participating agencies across six areas. These include verification of prescribed PTCS documents, recording of vehicle compliance status, identification of violations, initiation of enforcement or corrective measures, information exchange and data-sharing, as well as referral of cases requiring further administrative or regulatory action. Edu said commuter safety and security remained the primary reasons for strengthening regulation of public transportation in the state. He added that the ministry would engage transport unions and associations through stakeholder meetings, media campaigns and sensitisation programmes to ensure operators understood the requirements. The director further disclosed that the ministry had resolved to introduce continuous monitoring, evaluation and assessment of compliance levels across the state, supported by reporting and feedback mechanisms to ensure timely identification and resolution of regulatory gaps. item.title: “It was a prayer walk” – Adeboye clarifies controversy over alleged placard against Jonathan
item.description: The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Enoch Adeboye, has faulted media reports linking a placard he carried during a prayer walk to former President Goodluck Jonathan’s administration. The cleric spoke on Sunday during the church’s November Thanksgiving service, where he accused a journalist of misrepresenting the incident and portraying him as a wicked person for allegedly carrying a placard against the former president. Recounting how he came across the report, Adeboye said he was initially amused by the claim. “Recently, somebody wrote in the papers, or said somehow, ‘Pastor Adeboye is a very wicked man. After all, we know that not too long ago, he carried a placard against President Goodluck Jonathan,’” he said. While admitting that he carried a placard, the cleric insisted that the exercise was a prayer walk and not a protest against Jonathan. “True, I carried a placard. I can’t deny that. It was important. It was a prayer walk. We wanted to pray,” he said. He explained that the exercise followed a directive asking churches to organise prayer walks around their premises. “The chairman said all churches should do a prayer walk near their churches. That’s what I did,” he said. Adeboye further argued that the date of the exercise contradicted the report’s suggestion that he carried the placard against Jonathan while he was president. “But I carried the placard in 2020. Jonathan ceased to be president in 2015. I carried the placard five years in the second term of Buhari,” Adeboye said. He accused the journalist of distorting the facts and criticised the failure to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident before publishing the report. “But a journalist twisted it. I said, I did what I did in 2015. And everybody swallowed it,” he said. The RCCG leader also recalled his exposure to journalism studies in the 1960s, saying he was taught the importance of investigative journalism and verifying information before publication. “I remember in those days in the Department of Journalism, when you go there and you take a course, they talked about something called investigative journalism,” he said. He added, “That things don’t appear as they may seem. Investigate, if you have a story, before you take it to the press.” Vanguard News The post “It was a prayer walk” – Adeboye clarifies controversy over alleged placard against Jonathan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Vanguard, TVC, Channels, others fix November 8 for Lagos governorship debate
item.description: LAGOS — The Nigeria Debate Consortium has fixed November 8, 2026, for a governorship debate involving candidates contesting the 2027 Lagos State governorship election. The debate, scheduled for 7 p.m., will hold at The Hub by IALA, House of His Glory, Plot 18, Providence Road, beside Keystone Bank, Marwa, Lekki, Lagos. The consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, TheCable and Vanguard Newspaper, said the debate would kick-start its series of electoral engagements ahead of the 2027 general elections, covering selected battleground states before culminating in a presidential debate and town hall. In a statement announcing the event, the consortium said the initiative was designed to provide a credible, non-partisan platform for governorship candidates to present their agendas, defend their policy choices and respond to questions on issues affecting Lagos residents. It said the debate would focus on critical areas, including transportation, infrastructure, security, housing, education, healthcare, job creation and economic growth, allowing voters to assess the candidates’ proposals and readiness to govern. Channels Television said the initiative reflected the media’s responsibility to inform the electorate and strengthen democratic accountability. “Voters deserve more than campaign promises; they deserve clear answers, credible plans and an opportunity to assess those seeking their mandate,” the organisation said. It added that the debate would place issues, ideas and the future of Lagos at the centre of the electoral conversation, helping citizens make informed choices based on candidates’ proposals and their capacity to deliver. Similarly, TVC News described the debate as an opportunity for candidates to move beyond political rhetoric and demonstrate the substance of their vision for the state. “Citizens need to understand not only what candidates promise, but how they intend to deliver,” it said, adding that a fair platform for such engagement would promote accountability and an informed electorate. The consortium said the debate would be conducted in line with established professional standards, with fairness, neutrality, equal opportunity and editorial independence as guiding principles. It added that all participating candidates would be subjected to the same rules, speaking times and moderation standards. Experienced journalists are expected to moderate the debate, which will be broadcast to national and digital audiences through the participating media organisations’ platforms. The consortium called on Lagos residents, particularly eligible voters, young people, civil society organisations, professional groups and the business community, to follow the debate and engage with the issues and choices facing the state. The statement was jointly signed by Babajide Kolade-Otitoju, Director of News, TVC News, and Kingsley Uranta, General Manager, Channels Television. item.title: Germany ‘Gen Z Regelt’ Protest Turned Violent As Rioters Loot Shops
item.description: Masked rioters looted shops in the German city of Frankfurt on Saturday as massive demonstrations turned violent across the country, with police also firing water cannons at youths hurling Molotov cocktails. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined youth-led protests across the country organised by the group “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!). The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of young people refused to disperse, with violence breaking out in major cities including Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. It was especially bad in the financial hub of Frankfurt, where police faced protesters hurling stones, fireworks and petrol bombs, and responded with water cannon and pepper spray. “Violent riots” were taking place, police said in a statement. “Windows have been smashed at several shops. Molotov cocktails are also being thrown at emergency personnel.” Protesters light flares after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP) A gun store was among the shops looted, with its windows smashed. Police said they arrested a suspect and seized two weapons. A trainer shop and a perfume store were also targeted, the Bild daily reported. A large section of Frankfurt’s main shopping street was closed off as authorities sought to quell the unrest, with police vans and riot police stopping anyone from entering, according to an AFP journalist. A police helicopter hovered overhead as sporadic blasts were heard on the street. At least one police officer was injured there and was receiving medical treatment. ‘Shameful’ Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, said that “around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists” had infiltrated the protest in Frankfurt. “It is shameful how this event here in Frankfurt has ended.” Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. Riot Police block the street in front of protesters after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Photo by KIRILL KUDRYAVTSEV / AFP) In Berlin, a protest not organised by the “GenZ regelt!” movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles. A police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have arrested large numbers of rioters. The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere. Some people were dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween. item.title: Army rescues 11 kidnapped victims in Kebbi operations
item.description: Troops of Sector 2, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, have rescued 11 kidnapped victims in Danko-Wasagu Local Government Area of Kebbi in two separate encounters. The operations, deployed for counter-terrorism and anti-banditry, took place on Oct. 30 and 31. The Acting Deputy Director of Army Public Relations for 8 Division, Nigerian Army, Lt-Col. Osoba Olaniyi, confirmed this in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria in Birnin Kebbi on Sunday. He revealed that: “in the first operation, the troops responded to a distress call reporting that armed bandits have blocked a road leading to Ribah town and attempted to enter the town. “On arrival, troops found that an unspecified number of civilians have been kidnapped and some motorcycles were abandoned at the scene. “Troops immediately pursued the bandits and exchanged fire with them, forcing them to abandon seven kidnapped victims.” Olaniyi listed the rescued victims as Sa’adu Bala, Dantani Yahyi, Nura Musa, Nasiru Muhammad, Abdulakeem Abubakar, Abdulahi Maikudi and Zaki Gom. The acting director said the rescued persons had been reunited with their families. Speaking on the second operation, Olaniyi said the troops were on patrol in the Wasagu area when they came under fire from terrorists. “The troops responded decisively, forcing the terrorists to flee and abandon four victims who had earlier been abducted from their farms in Wasagu village. “The rescued victims were Lawali Ali, Samaila Shuaibu, Kasimu Shuaibu and Aliyu Bala, all of Wasagu village. They were handed over to the community head,” he said. Olaniyi reiterated the determination of the troops to the safety and security of all communities in the area, assuring that they would continue to respond promptly to security threats.
